A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same state-change counterfactual video representation framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original temporal action segmentation and error-detection experiments on GTEA and EgoPER, including component ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds recognition, retrieval, action-phase classification and human/model assessments of generated descriptions.

M1.justification: The proposed frame-, clip- and video-level alignment procedure, counterfactual generation prompts, frozen text encoder and training objectives remain unchanged. The additional downstream evaluations do not introduce a new representation-learning component.

E1.justification: v2 adds multi-instance retrieval on Epic-Kitchens, action recognition on Charades-Ego, and action-phase classification and frame retrieval on Align-Ego-Exo. These extend coverage to short-term tasks, egocentric/exocentric views and actions including tennis, while retaining EgoClip pretraining and GTEA/EgoPER evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained segmentation, error-detection and ablation experiments is unchanged. The new benchmarks use existing comparators CLIP, MIL-NCE and PVRL. 'Weak HierVL' names the existing ablation ID 1 rather than adding a comparator.

E3.justification: v2 introduces zero-shot text–vision evaluations, SVM action-phase classification and nearest-neighbor frame retrieval, merging Align-Ego-Exo validation and test sets. The ablation table drops F1@50 and Edit, retaining Acc and EDA. Appendix A.4 adds a 1–5 Likert evaluation with specified human and model sample sizes.

E4.justification: The six component configurations are retained, but their reported ablation evidence and findings are revised. Appendix A.4 adds a substantive supervision-quality assessment: 22 human raters assess 300 state-change/counterfactual pairs, and Gemini assesses 1,000, measuring relevance and plausibility. The original qualitative case studies are retained in Appendix B.2.

E5.justification: v1's ablation table reports single values without run counts or uncertainty. v2 Table 5 reports means and standard deviations across five runs for GTEA accuracy and ten for EgoPER EDA. These are newly reported counts, not evidence of an explicit increase from known earlier counts; the main benchmark tables retain single values.

E6.justification: New Tables 3–4 and 6–7 add substantial results, including the proposed method's Epic-Kitchens retrieval mAP of 15.7 and Charades-Ego recognition mAP of 24.8. The full-model ablation entries change from Acc 80.0/EDA 72.7 to 79.6±0.4/72.3±0.5 under separately documented settings and aggregation, rather than establishing a same-setting decline. Ablation F1/Edit entries disappear; Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the stated definition of HierVL's L_parent^ST from text-to-vision to text-to-text alignment. This is a limited revision to a background loss definition; the displayed equations and the proposed framework's mathematical formulation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the explicitly claimed demonstrated applicability from two procedural tasks to six procedural and short-term video tasks. The central contributions concerning state-change supervision, counterfactuals and hierarchical representation learning remain intact.

C2.justification: v1 interprets ablation ID 3 as supporting effective short-term error localization; v2 attributes its lower EDA than ID 2 to overfitting short-term procedures. v2 also adds a viewpoint-generalization interpretation and acknowledges that generated counterfactuals can depict low-probability scenarios, exposing a creativity–realism tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new downstream implementations and explains ID 1's use of other videos' narrations as negatives. It newly specifies batch size 12 per GPU for ablations alongside the retained general setting of 18; this does not establish what batch size v1's ablations actually used. Generation prompts and the promise of future code/data release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds limited citations, including ATARS, RiskBench, Charades-Ego and the Align-Ego-Exo work. The related-work organization and principal distinctions from HierVL, SCHEMA and earlier counterfactual approaches remain stable. Publication-detail updates to existing references do not represent new research positioning.

P1.justification: There are focused edits to the abstract, introduction and ablation discussion, additional experiment subsections and an acknowledgment section. The qualitative discussion moves from Section 4.5 to Appendix B.2. Most background, method exposition and existing appendix text are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds four benchmark tables and substantially restructures the ablation table around two metrics with mean±standard-deviation entries. Figures 3–4 move from the main text to the appendix with their content retained. Figures 1–2 and the original benchmark-table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Broader transfer evaluations, direct assessment of generated supervision and repeated-run uncertainty strengthen the empirical support beyond v1. Reporting regressions limit the gain: ablation F1/Edit results disappear while Section 4.6 still discusses them, and new retrieval summaries conflict—MIL-NCE is 59.5/63.0 in Table 4 but 53.0/54.2 in Table 7. The additional scrutiny provides a net benefit, but these inconsistencies and lost temporal-metric evidence prevent a substantial overall improvement.
